source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.17
text: Rice blast (ជំងឺផ្លាស់ / ជំងឺផ្សិតស្រូវ), a fungal disease, is a major risk at the nursery stage. It spreads via fungal spores and shows up as small lesions on leaves; the spores can be seen with a microscope. Contributing factors include sowing seed too densely/thickly on the nursery bed, and using seed that was itself harvested from a blast-infected field (carrying spores on the seed coat). Recommended prevention measures: select seed only from fields known to be disease-free; treat seed (e.g. with the hot-water or a chemical seed treatment) before sowing; avoid overly dense/crowded sowing on the nursery bed; scout the nursery regularly for early lesion symptoms; if disease appears, treat with a fungicide such as Sawant (active ingredient Isoprothiolane 40%); never re-use seed known to be infected; and remove/destroy severely infected nursery seedlings rather than transplanting them.
